LESSON: WRITING 6.3.1 CREATIVE WRITING

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 6
Topic 6.3: Writing 6.3.1 Creative Writing

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Writing 6.3.1 Creative Writing. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why are idioms important?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify idioms commonly used for information
2. use idioms to write an imaginative story
3. enjoy using idioms from their locality for language acquisition

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE LEARNING: WRITING 6.3.1 CREATIVE WRITING
This lesson teaches Writing 6.3.1 Creative Writing for Grade 5 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES.

STUDY STEPS
1. identify idioms commonly used for information
   Practise this until you can do it without help.
2. use idioms to write an imaginative story
   Practise this until you can do it without help.
3. enjoy using idioms from their locality for language acquisition
   Practise this until you can do it without help.

HOW TO SHOW UNDERSTANDING
Explain the idea in your own words, give one Kenyan example, then complete the practice tasks.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Describe Writing 6.3.1 Creative Writing using something at your school.

Example 2: Give a home/community example from your county.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Underline the key ideas about Writing 6.3.1 Creative Writing above.
2. Explain Writing 6.3.1 Creative Writing to a parent using one local example.
3. Write or draw three things that prove you understand Writing 6.3.1 Creative Writing.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Writing 6.3.1 Creative Writing with school or home examples.
2. Answer: Why is Writing 6.3.1 Creative Writing important for a Grade 5 learner?
3. Prepare a one-minute oral presentation for a parent or teacher.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why are idioms important?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. identify idioms commonly used for information
2. use idioms to write an imaginative story
3. enjoy using idioms from their locality for language acquisition

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
